scope: Every listed original PNG from the final sequential renderer checkpoint was individually displayed and reviewed by the release owner. These are component fixtures, not complete motocross playthrough images.

images.observation: The GP-R1 high model shows a complete red fairing, rider and striped helmet, winglets, fork, wheels, visible radial caliper and separated brake rotor surfaces. The front-quarter silhouette and ground shadow are coherent.
The mid model keeps the red fairing profile, rider pose, helmet striping, fork and wheel silhouettes. Brake and small body details are reduced as expected for this LOD.

The forced far model retains the motorcycle and tucked-rider silhouette with clearly simplified wheels, helmet and suit details. Its close presentation is a controlled LOD inspection, not the normal far-distance framing.
The GP-R2 high model has its distinct red upper and dark lower fairing, visible number, rider, fork and caliper. The different tail and side-body shapes remain intact.
The wet GP-R1 retains the same complete rider, fairing, wheel and brake assembly. The controlled material change is subtle in this neutral fixture; no claim of full wet-track lighting is made.
The restored dry GP-R1 returns to the first high-model appearance, including the fairing highlights, rider striping and ground shadow. Its PNG hash matches the initial dry capture.
The GP-R1 production camera has an unobstructed horizon above the windscreen. Gear 4, speed 151 and the RPM readout are legible on the dashboard; the screen edge overlaps its upper label area.
The GP-R2 camera retains a clear central forward horizon and its distinct windscreen and side-frame arrangement. Gear and speed remain readable through the translucent screen.
The SBK1000 production camera shows the dashboard below a clear forward horizon. Gear 4, speed 151 and RPM remain readable, with the windscreen passing over the upper dash region.
The SS600 dashboard, shift lights, gear, speed and RPM are legible below the forward view. Its screen top sits above the display without a rider head or torso obscuring the central corridor.
The initial same-instance weather capture shows the complete dry high model and rider with the original shadow and red fairing highlights.
The same model in the wet state retains all exterior parts and its coherent shadow. The material change does not displace the fairing, brake parts or rider.
The held wet frame repeats the previous wet model and shadow without visible drift. Its stored PNG hash is identical to the first wet frame.
The dry rewind restores the original same-instance exterior and shadow. Its stored PNG hash is identical to the initial dry frame.
